reports.title: Miles Robinson: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: In the UK, 999 calls are triaged using one of two approved triage tools (also referred to as call prioritisation systems) approved by NHS England: the Medical Priority Dispatch System ("MPDS") and NHS Pathways. LAS uses MPDS. The MPDS looks at signs and symptoms and prioritises them into dispatch codes, which assign a level of priority to the call, and in turn inform the type of ambulance resource that will be allocated to manage the incident
concerns.hazard: inaccurate triage of cardiac arrest symptoms

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that the MPDS triage system's rigid questioning fails to capture critical patient information, leading to under‑prioritisation of emergency calls.
links.earlier_quote: A call to the London Ambulance Service regarding a man who had been unconscious did not prompt a red prioritisation.
links.later_quote: Given the rigidity of the structured questions, there was no capacity within MPDS to account for information provided on behalf of Mr Robinson during the first 999 call, namely that he thought and felt like he was having a heart attack.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems in how emergency medical dispatchers assess whether a patient is conscious or unconscious, leading to incorrect assumptions. The later report shows the same issue persisting, affecting call prioritisation.
